subject: Retention and backup purge: proposed erase-window amendment / evidence request
messages:
From: Tara Singh <compliance@healthsync.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Retention alignment: backup rotation and emergency erase windows

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. HealthSync is finalizing our vendor due diligence for the next fiscal year and we have two related asks that came out of our Legal and Incident Response teams: 

1) We need clarity on the timeline and mechanics for backups and snapshot purges that may contain regulated data (PHI). Specifically: how long do primary snapshots persist, when are archives created, and how are snapshots purged from cold/offsite storage?

2) We need an emergency investigation hold option (up to 90 days) for forensic preserves when we trigger an ongoing incident response or legal investigation. Our standard DPA has a 90-day hold carveout but we need to understand whether Redwood can support that as an operational exception and what governance (signed amendment, evidence bundle) you require.

Quick context: we typically ask for a written amendment and a brief evidence bundle (SOC2 + snapshot retention map) before we agree to holds. Can you confirm: a) whether you support 90-day investigation holds; b) what the operational step-in looks like (how do you quiesce purge jobs / freeze TTLs); and c) whether backups may reside with a subprocessor we should be aware of.

Appreciate a short reply with a proposed next-step (MUTUAL ACTION PLAN) so our procurement team can circulate. CC'ing Oliver in case procurement needs to own the amendment.

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Head of Compliance, HealthSync
compliance@healthsync.ai

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

On Mon, Jan 9, 2028 at 09:12 AM Tara Singh <compliance@healthsync.ai> wrote:
> Hi Markus / Kimberly,
> 
> Thanks for taking this on. HealthSync is finalizing our vendor due diligence for the next fiscal year and we have two related asks...

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a temporary investigation hold up to 90 days, but it requires a narrow-scope amendment to the DPA and an operational acknowledgement (signed SOW addendum or DocuSign). We also require confirmation of the data classes in scope so we can identify which pipelines/snapshots are impacted.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Step 1 (Legal): Redwood drafts a short DPA amendment (language for emergency hold + subprocessor acknowledgement).
- Step 2 (Procurement): HealthSync reviews and returns a signed DocuSign.
- Step 3 (Product/Ops): Redwood freezes purge jobs for the scoped snapshots and provides an evidence bundle (snapshot index + retention map + SOC2 reference).
- Step 4 (Ops): Redwood maintains a quarantined copy for the specified 90-day period; after hold expiration we will follow agreed purge workflow unless instructed otherwise.

Operational notes (informal):
- Primary snapshot TTL: default 30 days for hot snapshots.
- Offsite/cold archive: rotated at 180 days (archival retention, read-only).
- Purge cadence: nightly TTL job that removes expired snapshots; archive deletion follows agreed schedule and may take up to 72 hours once triggered.

I'll attach a high-level backup map to show where artifacts live and which subprocessor buckets are used. Can someone from your side confirm whether the hold will cover "live snapshots only" or "all copies including cold archive"? The cold-archive carveout may require longer coordination with our storage subprocessor.

Proposing a short call Wed or Thu this week to finalize the amendment text and operational checklist.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention alignment: backup rotation and emergency erase windows

Hi Tara / Markus,

Thanks — I took a pass at redlined amendment language and attached a draft for HealthSync's review. Key points in the draft:

- Backup retention baseline: primary snapshots (hot) retained 30 days; archival layer retained 180 days.
- Investigation hold: customer may request a temporary hold up to 90 days for a named investigation; hold must be requested in writing and will be effective upon receipt of a signed amendment that defines scope (datasets, time ranges).
- Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list at the link in the footer of the DPA; backup storage may be hosted with our cloud storage subprocessor (name and region included in list).
- Evidence bundle required: SOC2 Type II attestation (most recent), snapshot index export (CSV), and high-level map of retention offsets for the scoped services.

Operational caveats: while we can freeze purge jobs for hot snapshots quickly, removing copies from cold/offsite archives requires coordination (typically 48–72 hours plus confirmation from the subprocessor). If HealthSync requires a hard guarantee that archives are also withheld, we need to specify that in the amendment and agree on an extended hold notice to the subprocessor.

I've attached the redline (dpa-amendment-draft.docx). Markus — can Product confirm the expected lead time for archive freeze and whether the team can provide the snapshot index format HealthSync requested?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Retention alignment: backup rotation and emergency erase windows

Hi all — looping in operational detail from the engineering side. Short technical answers below, and I included a small runbook snippet as an attachment so you can see the exact commands we run during a hold.

- Nightly purge job: runs 02:00 UTC, evaluates snapshot TTL, and enqueues deletions. Deletions for primary snapshots are executed asynchronously by the cleanup worker and are idempotent.
- Snapshot index export: we can produce a CSV that lists snapshot_id, creation_ts, storage_region, encryption_kms_key, subprocessor_bucket_id. Example column headers provided in the attached runbook snippet.
- Archive freeze: to prevent copies being removed from cold storage we mark the archive manifest as "quarantined" and issue a hold request to the storage subprocessor; typical subprocessor SLA to acknowledge and hold is 24–72 hours.
- Evidence package ETA: once amendment is signed we can deliver SOC2 reference link immediately, snapshot index within 3 business days, and the retention offset map within 48 hours.

Operational checklist (abridged):
1) Legal signoff (DocuSign)
2) Create internal hold ticket (INF-4127) — link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4127
3) Quiesce ingest pipelines that might churn the snapshots in-scope
4) Mark snapshot manifests as quarantined
5) Confirm subprocessor hold; export evidence bundle

I've attached purge-runbook-snippet.txt which contains the exact internal CLI commands we run for the first two steps. Happy to walk through the runbook on the call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Data Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Markus / Kimberly / Marissa — thanks for the quick and thorough responses. HealthSync is comfortable proceeding with the proposed path provided we get the following by next Wednesday (5 business days):

- Signed DPA amendment (DocuSign) with the explicit 90-day investigation hold clause.
- Evidence bundle: SOC2 Type II link, snapshot index CSV for the services listed below, and the retention offset map.
- Confirmation from Redwood that the subprocessor will acknowledge a quarantine request within 72 hours and will not run archive purge until confirmation is provided.

Scope for the amendment: Live API snapshots and analytics export snapshots from the last 6 months for the services named: api.healthsync.prod, analytics.ingest.prod.

If Redwood can confirm the above timeline (DocuSign + evidence bundle in 5 business days), Procurement will sign the amendment and we can schedule a short call to run the first hold test. Please also confirm whether you need any additional PO or billing terms changes — Oliver is copied for procurement coordination.

I'll expect the DocuSign link and a proposed call time.
